## Model Comparison {.unnumbered}

Three regression models are proposed for predicting house sale price.

All performance measures use the same dataset and the same cross-validation splits.

| Model | Predictors | Adj. $R^2$ | AIC | CV RMSE ($1,000s) | Max VIF | Diagnostics |
|:--|-------:|----:|--:|--:|--:|:-------------|
| A | 3 | 0.71 | 1240 | 31.5 | 2.1 | Good |
| B | 8 | 0.78 | 1208 | **27.9** | 8.7 | One moderately influential point |
| C | 15 + interactions | **0.80** | 1215 | 30.2 | 18.5 | Several unstable coefficients |

Lower AIC and lower CV RMSE are preferred.

## Which argument would you defend?

Three students make different claims.

**A.** "Model C is best because it has the largest adjusted $R^2$."

**B.** "Model B is best because it has the lowest cross-validation RMSE."

**C.** "Model A is best because it is the simplest and has the smallest VIF."

Which statement would you defend most strongly **for the prediction goal**?

Student: __________

Why?
